mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production (INDPRO) curve signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND INDPRO slope < 0 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered late-cycle episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above its 12-month moving average, accompanied by a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST), signals an expansion in manufacturing and construction capacity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA AND HOUST > 12-mo MA for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered supply-expansion episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail and food services sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average, without a corresponding drop in industrial production (INDPRO), signals a consumer confidence shock rather than a supply shock, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 6-mo MA for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO slope >= 0
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a tightening labor market that boosts wage pressure and consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average, coincident with a flattening GDP growth rate (GDPC1), signals a housing-market-led demand contraction, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-mo MA AND GDPC1 slope <= 0 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered housing downturn episodes.
